steps: Pressure cook the sprouted matki with a pinch of turmeric and some water for one whistle; keep the water.
Heat the oil, let the mustard and cumin seeds pop, then add the curry leaves and hing.
Fry most of the onion until light brown, then add the crushed ginger and garlic for a minute.
Add the tomato and salt and cook until soft and mushy.
Stir in the turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder and garam masala and fry until oil shows at the edges.
Add the matki with its water and more to make a thin curry, boil, then simmer for 10 minutes.
Slit the pav and toast it on a pan with the butter.
Ladle the misal into bowls, top with sev, raw onion, coriander and lemon, and serve with the pav.
note: After the 8-hour soak the matki needs about a day more wrapped in a damp cloth to sprout, so start two days ahead. Garam masala stands in for goda or misal masala, which the pack does not have, and sev stands in for farsan.
